blocks.x: Freshness-driven markdown on a demand spine — waste down 29% and markdown margin recovered without touching availability
a grocery chain whose fresh categories were managed by a markdown schedule printed in 2019. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter weighed the bins: 8.7% waste on fresh categories, markdown decisions made by calendar rather than by what was actually on the shelf, and availability protected by over-ordering that fed the waste.
Store teams marked down by rule-of-thumb, priced by feeling for what the morning would bring. Nobody could say which basket of rules worked because sell-through and waste never met in one report.

We built the fresh demand spine: store-level inventory, sell-through and waste data in one governed model with per-store per-SKU visibility, markdown recommendations priced from predicted daily demand curves, store teams approving within guardrails with overrides logged and scored, and waste-to-order feedback closing the loop upstream with buying.
